clue.text: Early Christian caught speaking out

indicators.note: speaking out means the word is said aloud, so we want a soundalike of it

parts.note: copped is slang for caught, as in caught by the police

explanation.surface: A member of the early Church is arrested for preaching openly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speaking out' signals a homophone: COPPED, slang for caught, sounds like COPT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Copts are the Egyptian Christians, a church dating from the first centuries AD.

clue.text: Inserting a page into message, it's accomplished

indicators.note: inserting means some letters are put inside another word
into names the word that receives the inserted letters

parts.note: a cable is a telegram, a message

explanation.surface: Someone who adds a page to a message is very able.
explanation.walkthrough: A and P go into CABLE, an old word for a telegram.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable and accomplished are synonyms, both meaning skilled and competent.

clue.text: Material for covering part of saint's limb

parts.note: St Peter's, belonging to the apostle
the ham is the back of the thigh, used here loosely for the leg

explanation.surface: Cloth used to wrap part of a holy man's leg.
explanation.walkthrough: Petersham is a heavy ribbed ribbon used to stiffen waistbands and hatbands, so it covers part of a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Petersham is a stiff corded ribbon or heavy cloth used in dressmaking and millinery.

clue.text: Almost from the start, English get on -—- honestly!

indicators.note: almost means the phrase is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: ab ovo is Latin for from the egg, meaning from the very beginning
to board a bus or train is to get on it

explanation.surface: An exclamation about getting aboard from the very beginning, done honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the final O of the Latin phrase ab ovo, literally 'from the egg', which English uses to mean from the very beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Above board is an idiom for openly and without deceit, so it can stand adverbially for honestly.

clue.text: Save cathedral city, but only just

parts.note: bar means save or except
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England

explanation.surface: Rescue a cathedral city, though with little to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' looks like rescue, but it means 'except'. ELY is a small English city with a famous cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Barely means by the narrowest margin, the same as only just.

clue.text: Viper, say, destroyed insect colony

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A snake, perhaps, wrecked a nest of insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges the letters of VIPER SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A vespiary is a nest of wasps, a colony of insects.

clue.text: Philosopher following tradition in part of London

parts.note: George Berkeley was an Irish idealist philosopher
square describes someone conventional who sticks to tradition

explanation.surface: A thinker who sticks to custom lives in a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' looks like a positional instruction, but 'following tradition' is the adjective SQUARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Berkeley Square is a famous square in Mayfair, so it is a place in London.

clue.text: Blue, not green

definitions.meaning: blue means pornographic, as in films for grown-ups only
not green means mature and experienced

explanation.surface: Something is blue rather than green.
explanation.definitionFit: Adult means explicit, like a blue film, and also grown-up rather than inexperienced.

clue.text: Ruin of the French city of Paris

parts.note: des is French for of the, plural
Paris was a prince of Troy in Greek legend

explanation.surface: The ruin of the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris' suggests France, but it is the Trojan prince, so his city is TROY.
explanation.definitionFit: Destroy and ruin are synonymous verbs meaning to wreck completely.

clue.text: One accompanying queen is shown to deliver this sting

definitions.text: One accompanying queen is shown to deliver this sting

parts.words: One accompanying queen is shown to deliver this sting
parts.note: a swindle where a card goes with the queen and the punter must find her as the cards are shuffled

explanation.surface: A card shown alongside a queen sets up a con.
explanation.walkthrough: The con, also called find the lady, uses a queen and two other cards; 'sting' is slang for a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a street gambling swindle in which punters bet on finding the queen among the cards.

clue.text: American sportsman that's able to hold a lot of beer

definitions.meaning: in baseball the player who throws the ball to the batter

definitions.text: that's able to hold a lot of beer
definitions.meaning: a large jug for serving drinks, often beer in America

explanation.surface: A US athlete who can drink a great deal of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the baseball thrower and the large jug used for serving beer.

clue.text: Composer of top rank covered with paste

indicators.note: covered with means one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: strass is paste, the glass used for imitation gems
U means upper class, the top social rank

explanation.surface: A top-ranking composer gets smeared with glue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered with' puts U (upper class) inside STRASS, a word for the paste used in fake jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Strauss and Richard Strauss are both famous composers by that surname.

clue.text: Nottingham and Lincoln do this for sheep

definitions.text: Nottingham and Lincoln do this for sheep

parts.words: Nottingham and Lincoln do this for sheep
parts.note: the counties of Nottingham and Lincoln lie next to Leicestershire, and the phrase saying so is also a breed of sheep

explanation.surface: Two English towns do something on behalf of sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: Nottinghamshire and Lincolnshire share a boundary with Leicestershire; the phrase is also the name of a British longwool sheep breed.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a hardy longwool breed of sheep developed on the English–Scottish borders.

clue.text: Code of behaviour of unnamed minority group

indicators.note: unnamed asks for N, the abbreviation for name, to be taken out

parts.note: ethnics is a noun for members of an ethnic minority

explanation.surface: A conduct code belonging to an anonymous minority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unnamed' removes N (name) from ETHNICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethics are the moral principles governing behaviour, a code of conduct.

clue.text: Ecclesiastical author heard but not seen

indicators.note: heard but not seen means we take the author's name as spoken, not as written

parts.note: J. B. Priestley was an English novelist and playwright

explanation.surface: A churchy writer who is heard but never seen, like a well-behaved child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard but not seen' signals a homophone: PRIESTLEY, the author of An Inspector Calls, sounds like PRIESTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Priestly means relating to priests, hence to the church, a close synonym of ecclesiastical.

clue.text: Continental representative aboard rescue vessel in leisure attraction

indicators.note: aboard means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the Ark was Noah's vessel for rescuing animals from the flood
an MEP is a Member of the European Parliament

explanation.surface: A European politician on a lifeboat at an amusement spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continental' points to the European Parliament; 'rescue vessel' is Noah's boat, with its article included.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme park is an amusement park built round a theme, a leisure attraction.

clue.text: Half of the men dance, some desperately get ready here

parts.note: pawns make up half the pieces, or men, in chess
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Half the men take to the floor while some get ready in desperation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is slang for cash: the desperate raise money at a pawnshop.
explanation.definitionFit: At a pawnbroker's the desperate get cash, 'ready money', by pledging goods.

clue.text: Injure back carrying gold on journey in doomed city

indicators.note: on means the rest is placed after the first piece

parts.note: go is a noun for a trip or turn, a journey

indicators.note: carrying means one piece holds another inside it
back means the word for injure is read backwards

parts.note: to harm is to injure
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone hurts their back lugging gold during a trip to a condemned city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word for injure (giving MRAH); 'carrying' sets the gold inside it, and 'on' puts all that after the journey. Or is the heraldic gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Gomorrah is the biblical city destroyed by God along with Sodom.

clue.text: Composer of sacred music for primates

definitions.meaning: Orlando ..., the English Tudor composer of church music

explanation.surface: A church music writer composes for apes.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlando Gibbons wrote church music; gibbons are also small apes.

clue.text: An expansion, in addition

definitions.meaning: read as two words, ... is ... or expansion
the phrase meaning also or too

explanation.surface: A swelling, plus something extra.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as A SWELL it is a swelling; as one phrase it means also, in addition.

clue.text: Flower-girl restricting the supply

indicators.note: restricting means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: Lily is both a flower and a girl's name

explanation.surface: A flower girl limits what is supplied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like the noun, but it is the adverb from supple, so it means nimbly.
explanation.definitionFit: Supply as the adverb of supple means flexibly, the same as lithely.

clue.text: Disgraceful mark of foreign character taking first of tests

indicators.note: taking means the letter is taken inside the word

parts.note: sigma is a Greek letter

indicators.note: first of selects the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A shameful mark on an alien taking the first of the exams.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside SIGMA, a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace or shame.

clue.text: Outspoken legal document produced in club, say

parts.note: blunt means frank and outspoken
an instrument is a formal legal document such as a deed

explanation.surface: A frankly worded legal paper is produced at a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a society, but it is the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A club is an example of a heavy weapon without an edge, the classic murder weapon.

clue.text: Remove bow of sailing vessel, say

indicators.note: the bow is the front of a ship, so its first letter is removed

parts.note: a cutter is a small single-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: Take off the front of a sailboat, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example', but it is the definition: UTTER. CUTTER loses its front letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to say or speak words aloud.

clue.text: Creature, with head concealed, most comical

indicators.note: with head concealed means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: rich can mean highly amusing, so most rich is most comical

explanation.surface: An animal hiding its head looks utterly ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rich' as in 'that's rich' means amusing; MOST RICH loses its first letter M. The surface nods to the ostrich's fabled head-burying.
explanation.definitionFit: An ostrich is a large flightless bird, an example of a creature.

clue.text: Material in European drug

parts.note: a German is a European
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Some substance found in a drug from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like a noun for stuff, but here it is the adjective meaning relevant.
explanation.definitionFit: Material in the sense of relevant or pertinent is a synonym of germane.

clue.text: Gamble on piece of writing as one way to compete on course

definitions.text: one way to compete on course

indicators.note: on means the gamble is placed after the piece of writing

parts.note: a stroke is a single mark made with a pen
to play is to gamble

explanation.surface: Betting on a written work as a way of competing on a racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of writing' suggests an essay, but it is one pen STROKE; 'course' is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroke play is a golf format scored by total strokes, one way to compete on a golf course.

clue.text: Agree fine dessert wine must remain unopened

indicators.note: unopened means the word loses its first letter, as a bottle keeps its top

parts.note: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian dessert wine

explanation.surface: Consent that a good sweet wine should stay corked.
explanation.walkthrough: TOKAY, the Hungarian dessert wine, loses its opening T.
explanation.definitionFit: To okay something is to approve it, so it works as a verb meaning agree.
